vantageRuleApplication.whyTheRuleDoesNotApplyToEitherFailure: clause 1 requires a pre-socket BLOCKED_BY_POLICY refusal by the landed address classifier over an address that resolution DID return. Neither failure produced one. R:64:23 resolved its host and then failed the TLS handshake; P:65 failed to RESOLVE its target name at all. A resolution failure and a handshake failure are both categorically different from the classifier refusing a translated address
vantageRuleApplication.aTlsFailureIsNotANat64Refusal: TLS_PROTOCOL_INCOMPATIBLE is a property of the peer server TLS configuration, observed after a successful connect. Nothing about it is an environment artefact of this vantage
vantageRuleApplication.aDnsFailureIsNotANat64Refusal: this distinction is the reason the rule enumerates five conjunctive clauses rather than keying on zero-yield
